option_relations.rationale: The vignette describes syncope and exertional fatigue, but the ECG findings (prolonged PR, prolonged QRS, left axis deviation) and Holter monitoring (regular rhythm, no pauses) do not strongly suggest ventricular tachyarrhythmia as the primary cause of syncope. The provided leaf is about intermittent complete AV block.

Advanced conduction system disease is a broader category that encompasses intermittent complete atrioventricular block, which is the specific condition described in the leaf. The ECG findings (prolonged PR, prolonged QRS, left axis deviation) are consistent with advanced conduction system disease.

Complete heart block (trifascicular block) is a specific type of advanced conduction system disease that can lead to intermittent complete atrioventricular block, which is the condition described in the leaf. The ECG findings (prolonged PR, prolonged QRS, left axis deviation) are highly suggestive of trifascicular block.

Masquerading bundle-branch block (MBBB) with progression to advanced atrioventricular block is a specific form of conduction system disease that can result in intermittent complete atrioventricular block, as described in the leaf. The ECG findings (prolonged QRS, Morris index in V1, notched and monophasic R-wave in V1, absent S wave in I and aVL, left axis deviation) are characteristic of MBBB.
